title: Patriots sign former Giants defensive tackle Casey Rogers
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: The New England Patriots signed defensive tackle Casey Rogers, formerly on the Giants' and Bills' practice squads.
Rogers, 27, played in 10 games with the DC Defenders in the United Football League, recording 21 tackles and 1.5 sacks.
Rogers was present at Patriots practice in Foxborough, joining a strong defensive line group on the 90-player preseason roster.

title: 5 things to know about new Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Boston Red Sox acquire catcher Adley Rutschman from Baltimore Orioles, sending Carlos Narvaez and prospects in exchange.
Rutschman, 28, has battled injuries recently but remains a defensive asset with a .251 batting average this season.
Rutschman was the No. 1 pick in 2019 MLB Draft, known for his hitting prowess and defensive skills.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 8 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: A.J. Brown played through a dislocated thumb, making key catches during red-zone drills.
Efton Chism had a standout day, catching multiple touchdowns during scrimmages.
Undrafted cornerback Channing Canada impressed with pass breakups and involvement in kick return drills.

title: Ballot Brief: Your guide to the 2026 midterms
author: Zipporah Osei
bullets: Ballot Brief newsletter provides key updates on the 2026 Massachusetts midterms including governor and U.S. Senate races.
Early voting starts August 22 with primaries on September 1 in Massachusetts for the 2026 midterm elections.
Subscribers receive analysis of debates, ballot question explanations, and essential voting information before Election Day.

title: Somerville man accused of World Cup ticket scam that netted $14K
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Robert Whelan, 50, of Somerville, faces charges for an alleged $14,000 World Cup ticket scam.
Whelan allegedly promised tickets using false claims of priority access through the Patriots season ticket privileges.
Arraigned in Somerville District Court, Whelan's bail was set at $250, with his next court appearance on September 23.

title: Man charged with kidnapping, raping door-to-door salesperson in Everett
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 67-year-old Everett man, James Mugford, was charged with kidnapping and raping a door-to-door salesperson.
Mugford allegedly threatened the victim with weapons at his Fremont Avenue home and held her against her will.
He was arraigned on charges including aggravated rape and is held without bail; court date set for August 28.

title: Red Sox acquire catcher Adley Rutschman from Orioles
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox acquired catcher Adley Rutschman and Jake Rogers from the Orioles before the MLB trade deadline.
Boston sent Carlos Narvaez, Anthony Eyanson, Kyson Witherspoon, Enddy Azocar, and considerations to Baltimore in the trade.
Rutschman, a three-time All-Star, has a .251 average with eight home runs this season despite injury setbacks.

title: The top four fall foliage destinations in the U.S. are not in New England, according to Priceline
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Priceline's top four U.S. fall foliage spots include areas in New York, Washington, Colorado, and Pennsylvania.
New England destinations ranked lower, with Bretton Woods, Berkshires, and Stowe at fifth, eighth, and ninth positions.
The Adirondacks in New York claimed the top spot for fall foliage in Priceline's 2026 list.

title: Bruce Springsteen, whose wife was treated in Boston, salutes Pan-Mass Challenge participants
author: Peter Chianca
bullets: Bruce Springsteen praised Pan-Mass Challenge participants during a video address at the State of PMC program in Worcester.
Springsteen's wife, Patti Scialfa, treated for multiple myeloma in Boston, contributed to his support for the event.
The annual Pan-Mass Challenge bike ride benefits cancer research at Dana-Farber, raising over $1 billion since 1980.

title: 1 dead, 4 injured in overnight Hyde Park shooting
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A shooting in Hyde Park left one dead and four injured early Monday, according to Boston police.
The shooting occurred around 12:38 a.m. at 1184 Hyde Park Ave; all victims were hospitalized.
Boston Police Homicide Unit is investigating; tips can be submitted anonymously at 1-800-494-8477.
